translations.idiomatic: Now that the four guard regions lay beyond the frontier and the Five Peaks stood within the inner commanderies, it was fitting to broaden the rites of ceding the throne below and enrich the teachings of the feng sacrifice above, leaving the pure capital behind by day and turning toward the cloud-wreathed suburbs in solemn procession.

sentences.zh: 將絕塵而弭轍，類飛鳥與駏驢。

translations.literal: About to leave the dust behind and stop the wheel tracks, resembling flying birds and zebras.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage would leave the dust behind and halt its tracks, swift as a flying bird beside a zebra.

sentences.zh: 總三才而驅騖，按五御而超攄。

translations.literal: Gathering the three powers and driving in gallop, pressing the five imperial steeds and leaping beyond.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering heaven, earth, and humanity in one galloping drive, he would guide the five imperial horses and surge beyond all bounds.

sentences.zh: 翳卿雲於華蓋，翼條風於屬車。

translations.literal: Screening ministerial clouds upon the imperial canopy, winging the gentle wind upon the retinue carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious clouds would shade the imperial canopy, and gentle winds would wing the train of attendant carriages.

sentences.zh: 無逸御於玉軫，不泛駕於金輿。

translations.literal: Without excessive driving upon the jade axle, without over-driving upon the golden carriage.
translations.idiomatic: There would be no reckless handling of the jade axles, no overtaxing of the golden chariot.

sentences.zh: 飾中岳之絕軌，營奉高之舊墟。

translations.literal: Adorning the supreme tracks of the Central Peak, building at the old site of Fenggao.
translations.idiomatic: He would adorn the sacred paths of Mount Song and restore the ancient altar at Fenggao.

sentences.zh: 訓厚況於人神，弘施育於黎獻。

translations.literal: Teaching thick blessings upon humans and spirits, broadly extending nurture to the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: His instruction would deepen blessings for both men and gods, and his bounty would broadly nourish the people.

sentences.zh: 垂景炎於長世，集繁祉於斯萬，在庸臣之方剛，有從軍之大願。

translations.literal: Hanging blazing glory upon long generations, gathering abundant blessings for this myriad—this mediocre official, upright and strong, has a great wish to follow the army.
translations.idiomatic: His blazing glory would shine through long ages and gather abundant blessings for the myriad people; as for this humble servant, still firm in his prime, I harbor the great wish to follow the imperial host.

sentences.zh: 必自茲而展采，將同畀於庖煇。

translations.literal: Surely from this one will display one's colors, and will share bestowment with the kitchen smoke.
translations.idiomatic: Surely from that moment I would display my talents and share in the offerings rising from the sacrificial hearth.

sentences.zh: 悼長卿之遺書，憫周南之留恨。

translations.literal: Mourning Changqing's posthumous writings, pitying the lingering regret of Zhou Nan.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve for Sima Xiangru's testament left unfinished and pity the sorrow Zhou Nan could not lay to rest.

sentences.zh: 時與到洽、周興嗣同奉詔爲賦，高祖以率及興嗣爲工。

translations.literal: At the time he together with Dao Qia and Zhou Xingsi received the edict to compose fu; Emperor Gaozu regarded Shuai and Xingsi as the skilled ones.
translations.idiomatic: At that time he, together with Dao Qia and Zhou Xingsi, received an edict to compose rhapsodies; Emperor Gaozu judged Shuai and Xingsi the finest craftsmen among them.

sentences.zh: 其年，父憂去職。

translations.literal: That year, on father's bereavement he left office.
translations.idiomatic: That year he resigned his post to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 其父侍妓數十人，善謳者有色貌，邑子儀曹郎顧玩之求娉焉，謳者不願，遂出家爲尼。

translations.literal: His father had several dozen attendant courtesans; one skilled at singing was beautiful in appearance. A fellow townsman, Gu Wanzhi, an aide in the Bureau of Rites, sought to marry her; the singer was unwilling and thereupon left home to become a nun.
translations.idiomatic: His father kept several dozen courtesans; among them a singer of exceptional beauty caught the eye of a fellow townsman, Gu Wanzhi, an aide in the Bureau of Rites, who sought her hand in marriage. She refused, and in the end took the tonsure and became a nun.

sentences.zh: 嘗因齋會率宅，玩之乃飛書言與率姦，南司以事奏聞，高祖惜其才，寢其奏，然猶致世論焉。

translations.literal: Once, because of a fast-day gathering at Shu's residence, Wanzhi sent a flying letter alleging an affair with Shu; the Southern Office reported the matter to the throne. Emperor Gaozu valued his talent and suppressed the memorial, yet it still provoked public talk.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion a fasting assembly was held at Shu's home, and Wanzhi sent an urgent letter accusing Shu of adultery with the singer. The Southern Office reported the matter to the throne; Emperor Gaozu, cherishing Shu's talent, shelved the memorial, but the affair still stirred public gossip.

sentences.zh: 服闋後，久之不仕。

translations.literal: After the mourning period ended, for a long time he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, he went a long time without taking up office again.

sentences.zh: 七年，敕召出，除中權建安王中記室參軍，預長名問訊，不限日。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, by edict he was summoned forth and appointed Middle Recorder on the staff of the Prince of Jian'an under Central Authority; he participated in changming inquiries without a day limit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year an edict summoned him back to service, appointing him Middle Recorder on the staff of the Prince of Jian'an under Central Authority; he was included in changming inquiries with no fixed term.

sentences.zh: 俄有敕直壽光省，治丙丁部書抄。

translations.literal: Soon there was an edict assigning him directly to the Shouguang Office to compile copies of the bingding section books.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict posted him directly to the Shouguang Office to compile copies from the bing and ding sections of the archives.

sentences.zh: 八年，晉安王戍石頭，以率爲雲麾中記室。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the Prince of Jin'an garrisoned Stone City, Shu was made Middle Recorder under the Cloud Banner command.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when the Prince of Jin'an took up the garrison at Stone City, Shu was appointed Middle Recorder on his Cloud Banner staff.

sentences.zh: 王遷南兗州，轉宣毅諮議參軍，並兼記室。

translations.literal: When the prince transferred to South Yanzhou, Shu became Consultative Military Attendant under Xuanyi and also concurrently served as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince moved to South Yanzhou, Shu was transferred to Consultative Military Attendant under the Xuanyi command and also retained his post as recorder.

sentences.zh: 王還都，率除中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When the prince returned to the capital, Shu was appointed Gentleman of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince returned to the capital, Shu was appointed Gentleman of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十三年，王爲荊州，復以率爲宣惠諮議，領江陵令。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the prince went to Jingzhou, Shu was again made Xuanhui Consultative Attendant and concurrently served as magistrate of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when the prince took up his post in Jingzhou, Shu was again appointed Consultative Attendant under the Xuanhui command and concurrently served as magistrate of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 王爲江州，以諮議領記室，出監豫章、臨川郡。

translations.literal: When the prince went to Jiangzhou, Shu as consultative attendant also led the recorder's office and went out to supervise Yuzhang and Linchuan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince moved to Jiangzhou, Shu served as consultative attender and chief recorder, and was sent out to supervise the commanderies of Yuzhang and Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 率在府十年，恩禮甚篤。

translations.literal: Shu was in the prince's staff for ten years; grace and courtesy were very deep.
translations.idiomatic: Shu served on the prince's staff for ten years, and the favor and courtesy shown him were exceptionally warm.

sentences.zh: 率嗜酒，事事寬恕，于家務尤忘懷。

translations.literal: Shu loved wine, in all matters was forgiving, and especially forgot household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was fond of wine, forgiving in all things, and especially heedless of household affairs.

sentences.zh: 在新安，遣家僮載米三千石還吳宅，旣至，遂秏太半。

translations.literal: While in Xin'an, he sent a household servant to carry three thousand shi of rice back to his Wu residence; when it arrived, more than half had been consumed.
translations.idiomatic: While stationed in Xin'an, he sent a household servant to transport three thousand shi of rice back to his home in Wu; by the time it arrived, more than half was gone.

sentences.zh: 率問其故，答曰：「雀鼠秏也。

translations.literal: Shu asked the reason, and the answer came: "Sparrows and mice consumed it."
translations.idiomatic: Shu asked what had happened, and the servant replied, "Sparrows and mice ate it."

sentences.zh: 」率笑而言曰：「壯哉雀鼠。

translations.literal: " Shu smiled and said: "How mighty the sparrows and mice!"
translations.idiomatic: " Shu laughed and said, "What formidable sparrows and mice!"

sentences.zh: 」竟不研問。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not investigate further.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he never pursued the matter.

sentences.zh: 少好屬文，而《七略》及《藝文志》所載詩賦，今亡其文者，並補作之。

translations.literal: From youth he loved literary composition; as for the poetry and fu listed in the Qilüe and the Yiwen zhi whose texts are now lost, he all supplemented and composed them.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved to write, and for every poem and rhapsody listed in the Qilüe and the Yiwen zhi whose text was now lost, he composed a replacement.

sentences.zh: 所著《文衡》十五卷，文集三十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: His Wenheng in fifteen juan and collected works in thirty juan circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Literary Balance in fifteen scrolls and his collected works in thirty scrolls circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子長公嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chang succeeded to the title of duke.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang inherited the ducal title.

sentences.zh: 劉孝綽字孝綽，彭城人，本名冉。

translations.literal: Liu Xiaochuo, styled Xiaochuo, was a native of Pengcheng; his original name was Ran.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaochuo, styled Xiaochuo, came from Pengcheng; his original given name was Ran.

sentences.zh: 祖勔，宋司空忠昭公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xun was Song Minister of Works, Duke Zhongzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xun was Minister of Works under the Song and was posthumously ennobled as Duke Zhongzhao.

sentences.zh: 父繪，齊大司馬霸府從事中郎。

translations.literal: His father Hui was Attendant Gentleman on the staff of the Qi Grand Marshal's hegemonic office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui served as Attendant Gentleman on the staff of the Qi Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 孝綽幼聰敏，七歲能屬文。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo was clever from childhood; at seven he could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo was bright as a child and could write polished prose by the age of seven.

sentences.zh: 舅齊中書郎王融深賞異之，常與同載適親友，號曰神童。

translations.literal: His maternal uncle Wang Rong, Gentleman of the Central Secretariat under Qi, deeply admired and regarded him as extraordinary; he often rode in the same carriage with him to visit friends and relatives, and called him a divine child.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal uncle Wang Rong, a Gentleman of the Central Secretariat under Qi, admired him greatly and often took him along in his carriage to visit friends and kin, calling him a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 融每言曰：「天下文章，若無我當歸阿士。

translations.literal: Rong often said: "Under heaven's literature, if not for me it should go to A-shi."
translations.idiomatic: Rong often said, "Of all the writers under heaven, if not for me the crown would belong to A-shi."

sentences.zh: 」阿士，孝綽小字也。

translations.literal: " A-shi was Xiaochuo's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: " A-shi was Xiaochuo's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 繪，齊世掌詔誥。

translations.literal: Hui, during the Qi dynasty, managed imperial edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qi, Hui was in charge of drafting imperial edicts and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 孝綽年未志學，繪常使代草之。

translations.literal: Before Xiaochuo had reached the age of zhi learning, Hui often had him draft them in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xiaochuo had even reached the age of formal study, Hui regularly had him draft the documents instead.

sentences.zh: 父黨沈約、任昉、范雲等聞其名，並命駕先造焉，昉尤相賞好。

translations.literal: His father's associates Shen Yue, Ren Fang, Fan Yun, and others heard his name and all ordered their carriages to visit him first; Fang especially admired and befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: His father's friends Shen Yue, Ren Fang, Fan Yun, and others heard of him and all came calling before anyone else; Ren Fang in particular admired and befriended him.

sentences.zh: 范雲年長繪十餘歲，其子孝才與孝綽年並十四五，及雲遇孝綽，便申伯季，乃命孝才拜之。

translations.literal: Fan Yun was more than ten years older than Hui; his son Xiaocai and Xiaochuo were both fourteen or fifteen. When Yun met Xiaochuo, he at once proposed elder-younger brotherhood and then ordered Xiaocai to bow to him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun was more than ten years Hui's senior; his son Xiaocai and Xiaochuo were both fourteen or fifteen. When Yun met Xiaochuo, he immediately proposed a bond of elder and younger brother and had Xiaocai bow to him.

sentences.zh: 天監初，起家著作佐郎，爲《歸沐詩》以贈任昉，昉報章曰：「彼美洛陽子，投我懷秋作。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, he began his career as Associate Archivist and wrote the "Poem on Returning to Bathe" to present to Ren Fang; Fang replied in verse, saying: "That fair gentleman of Luoyang sends me autumn sentiments in writing."
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianjian era he entered service as Associate Archivist and wrote "Poem on Returning to Bathe" as a gift for Ren Fang; Fang replied with a poem that began, "That fair gentleman of Luoyang sends me verses steeped in autumn feeling."

sentences.zh: 詎慰耋嗟人，徒深老夫託。

translations.literal: How can it comfort an old man who sighs? It only deepens this old man's trust.
translations.idiomatic: Can such lines truly comfort an old man given to lament? They only deepen the trust this old man places in you.

sentences.zh: 直史兼褒貶，轄司專疾惡。

translations.literal: The straight historian both praises and blames; the governing office specially hates evil.
translations.idiomatic: A faithful historian both praises and condemns, and the office that governs him especially despises wickedness.

sentences.zh: 九折多美疹，匪報庶良藥。

translations.literal: Nine bends have many fine marks; not replying, perhaps, is good medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Many a winding path leaves fine traces; even silence, perhaps, may prove the better remedy.

sentences.zh: 子其崇鋒穎，春耕勵秋獲。

translations.literal: You should honor sharp talent; spring plowing encourages autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Honor your sharp gifts, plow in spring, and strive for the autumn yield.

sentences.zh: 」其爲名流所重如此。

translations.literal: " Thus he was esteemed by famous men.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which leading men held him.

sentences.zh: 遷太子舍人，俄以本官兼尚書水部郎，奉啓陳謝，手敕答曰：「美錦未可便制，簿領亦宜稍習。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant of the Crown Prince; soon, retaining his original post, he also served as Gentleman of the Water Section in the Ministry of Works. He submitted a memorial declining, and a handwritten edict replied: "Beautiful brocade cannot yet be made at once; registers and ledgers should also be slightly learned."
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant of the Crown Prince and soon added the concurrent post of Gentleman of the Water Section in the Ministry of Works. When he submitted a memorial declining the appointment, the Emperor answered in his own hand, "Fine brocade cannot be woven all at once; you should also gain some familiarity with paperwork."

sentences.zh: 」頃之卽真。

translations.literal: " Before long he received the regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he received the regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 高祖雅好蟲篆，時因宴幸，命沈約、任昉等言志賦詩，孝綽亦見引。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu elegantly loved ancient seal script; at times during banquets and imperial visits he ordered Shen Yue, Ren Fang, and others to speak their aspirations and compose fu and poetry; Xiaochuo was also summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu had a refined taste for ancient seal script, and during banquets and imperial outings he would summon Shen Yue, Ren Fang, and others to speak their minds and compose poetry and rhapsodies; Xiaochuo was invited as well.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴，於坐爲詩七首，高祖覽其文，篇篇嗟賞，由是朝野改觀焉。

translations.literal: Once while attending a banquet he composed seven poems on the spot; Emperor Gaozu read his writings and admired each one; from this court and countryside changed their view of him.
translations.idiomatic: On one banquet occasion he composed seven poems on the spot; the Emperor read each one with admiration, and from that day both court and countryside revised their opinion of him.

sentences.zh: 尋有敕知青、北徐、南徐三州事，出爲平南安成王記室，隨府之鎮。

translations.literal: Soon there was an edict assigning him to know the affairs of Qing, North Xu, and South Xu—the three prefectures; he went out as recorder to the Prince of Pingnan, Prince of Ancheng, and followed the prince's staff to the post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict put him in charge of affairs in Qingzhou and the northern and southern Xu prefectures; he then went out as recorder to the Prince of Pingnan, Prince of Ancheng, and accompanied the prince to his post.

sentences.zh: 尋補太子洗馬，遷尚書金部侍郎，復爲太子洗馬，掌東宮管記。

translations.literal: Soon he was supplemented as Crown Prince Groom, transferred to Vice Minister of the Gold Section in the Ministry of Works, again made Crown Prince Groom, and managed the Eastern Palace records.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed supplemental Crown Prince Groom, then promoted to Vice Minister of the Gold Section, and afterward returned to the post of Crown Prince Groom, where he managed the Eastern Palace records.

sentences.zh: 出爲上虞令，遷除秘書丞。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Shangyu, then was transferred and removed to serve as Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Shangyu, then was promoted to Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂舍人周捨曰：「第一官當用第一人。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said to Attendant Zhou She: "The foremost office should employ the foremost man."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu told Attendant Zhou She, "The foremost office ought to go to the foremost man."

sentences.zh: 」故以孝綽居此職。

translations.literal: " Therefore Xiaochuo was placed in this office.
translations.idiomatic: " For that reason Xiaochuo was given the post.

sentences.zh: 公事免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for a public-affairs offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for an official offense.

sentences.zh: 尋復除秘書丞，出爲鎮南安成王諮議，入以事免。

translations.literal: Soon he was again appointed Assistant Director of the Secretariat, went out as consultative attender to the Prince of Zhennan, Prince of Ancheng, and upon returning was dismissed because of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed Assistant Director of the Secretariat, then sent out as consultative attender to the Prince of Zhennan, Prince of Ancheng; when he returned to court he was dismissed because of the affair.

sentences.zh: 起爲安西記室，累遷安西驃騎諮議參軍，敕權知司徒右長史事，遷太府卿、太子僕，復掌東宮管記。

translations.literal: He was raised up as recorder under Anxi, accumulated promotions to Consultative Military Attendant under the Anxi Cavalry General, by edict was temporarily placed in charge of the Master of the East Department's Right Chief Clerk affairs, was transferred to Grand Steward and Crown Prince Steward, and again managed the Eastern Palace records.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as recorder on the Anxi staff, rose through successive posts to Consultative Military Attendant under the Anxi Cavalry General, was by edict temporarily placed in charge of the Right Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Civil Affairs, then promoted to Grand Steward and Crown Prince Steward, and again took charge of the Eastern Palace records.

sentences.zh: 時昭明太子好士愛文，孝綽與陳郡殷芸、吳郡陸倕、琅邪王筠、彭城到洽等，同見賓禮。

translations.literal: At the time Crown Prince Zhaoming loved scholars and cherished literature; Xiaochuo, together with Yin Yun of Chen commandery, Lu Chuo of Wu commandery, Wang Jun of Langya, Dao Qia of Pengcheng, and others, all equally received guest courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Crown Prince Zhaoming loved men of talent and cherished literature; Xiaochuo, together with Yin Yun of Chen, Lu Chuo of Wu, Wang Jun of Langya, Dao Qia of Pengcheng, and others, all received the same honored treatment as guests.

sentences.zh: 太子起樂賢堂，乃使畫工先圖孝綽焉。

translations.literal: The crown prince built Lexian Hall and then had the painters first depict Xiaochuo there.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince built the Hall of Delighting in Worthies, he had the painters depict Xiaochuo there first.

sentences.zh: 太子文章繁富，羣才咸欲撰錄，太子獨使孝綽集而序之。

translations.literal: The crown prince's literary works were abundant and rich; all the assembled talents wished to compile and record them, but the crown prince alone had Xiaochuo collect and preface them.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's literary output was vast, and many talented men wished to compile it, but the crown prince entrusted that task to Xiaochuo alone, who collected the pieces and wrote the preface.

sentences.zh: 遷員外散騎常侍，兼廷尉卿，頃之卽真。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supernumerary Regular Cavalry Attendant and concurrently served as Minister of Justice; before long he received the regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supernumerary Regular Cavalry Attendant with concurrent appointment as Minister of Justice, and soon received the regular post.

sentences.zh: 初，孝綽與到洽友善，同遊東宮。

translations.literal: Initially Xiaochuo and Dao Qia were friendly and together visited the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xiaochuo and Dao Qia were on friendly terms and frequented the Eastern Palace together.

sentences.zh: 孝綽自以才優於洽，每於宴坐，嗤鄙其文，洽銜之。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo considered himself more talented than Qia; at every banquet gathering he mocked and despised Qia's writings, and Qia harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo believed himself more gifted than Qia and, at every banquet, openly scorned his writing; Qia took deep offense.

sentences.zh: 及孝綽爲廷尉卿，攜妾入官府，其母猶停私宅。

translations.literal: When Xiaochuo became Minister of Justice, he brought a concubine into the official residence while his mother still remained at the private home.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaochuo became Minister of Justice, he brought a concubine into his official quarters while his mother remained in their private residence.

sentences.zh: 洽尋爲御史中丞，遣令史案其事，遂劾奏之，云：「攜少妹於華省，棄老母於下宅。

translations.literal: Qia soon became Censor-in-Chief, sent a clerk to investigate the matter, and thereupon impeached him, saying: "He brings a young sister into the splendid office and abandons his old mother in the lower residence."
translations.idiomatic: Qia was soon appointed Censor-in-Chief, sent a clerk to investigate, and impeached him with the charge, "He brings a young woman into the imperial offices while leaving his aged mother in a humble dwelling."

sentences.zh: 」高祖爲隱其惡，改「妹」爲「姝」。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu, to hide his shame, changed "younger sister" to "concubine."
translations.idiomatic: " To conceal the scandal, Emperor Gaozu altered the word for "younger sister" to the word for "concubine."

sentences.zh: 坐免官。

translations.literal: Because of the offense he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed from office on that charge.

sentences.zh: 孝綽諸弟，時隨籓皆在荊、雍，乃與書論共洽不平者十事，其辭皆鄙到氏。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo's younger brothers, at the time following the princes, were all in Jing and Yong; he therefore wrote them a letter discussing ten grievances shared against Qia, and the wording all derided the Dao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo's younger brothers were then serving with princes in Jing and Yong; he wrote them a letter listing ten grievances they held against Qia, and every line disparaged the Dao family.

sentences.zh: 又寫別本封呈東宮，昭明太子命焚之，不開視也。

translations.literal: He also copied a separate version, sealed it, and presented it to the Eastern Palace; Crown Prince Zhaoming ordered it burned without opening and reading it.
translations.idiomatic: He also made a separate copy, sealed it, and sent it to the Eastern Palace; Crown Prince Zhaoming ordered it burned unread.

sentences.zh: 時世祖出爲荊州，至鎮，與孝綽書曰：「君屏居多暇，差得肆意典墳，吟詠情性，比復稀數古人，不以委約而能不伎癢；

translations.literal: At the time Prince Shiyizu went out to Jingzhou; upon reaching his post he wrote to Xiaochuo, saying: "You, dwelling in retirement, have much leisure and can freely indulge in the classics, chanting and expressing your nature. Recently you again rarely count the ancients—not because you are constrained and yet unable to resist the itch for writing;"
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Shiyizu had been sent to Jingzhou, and upon reaching his post he wrote to Xiaochuo: "Retired at home, you have ample leisure to roam freely among the classics and give voice to your temperament. Of late you have seldom measured yourself against the ancients—not because restraint keeps you from scratching the writer's itch;"

sentences.zh: 且虞卿、史遷由斯而作，想摛屬之興，益當不少。

translations.literal: Moreover, Yu Qing and Shi Qian arose from this; I think the impulse to compose must be no small thing.
translations.idiomatic: After all, men like Yu Qing and Sima Qian were born of just such impulses; surely your urge to write has only grown stronger.

sentences.zh: 洛地紙貴，京師名動，彼此一時，何其盛也。

translations.literal: In Luoyang paper grew costly; in the capital one's name stirred—each at its moment; how splendid!
translations.idiomatic: Paper grew costly in Luoyang and your name resounded in the capital—you and your peers each had your hour; what a glorious season that was!

sentences.zh: 近在道務閑，微得點翰，雖無紀行之作，頗有懷舊之篇。

translations.literal: Recently on the journey duties have been idle; I have slightly been able to touch the brush. Although there are no travel-record compositions, there are quite a few nostalgic pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, on the road, my duties have been lighter and I have managed a little writing; though I have produced no travel chronicle, I have composed several pieces steeped in nostalgia.

sentences.zh: 至此已來，衆諸屑役。

translations.literal: Since arriving here until now, a multitude of petty duties.
translations.idiomatic: Since my arrival here, I have been buried in a swarm of petty tasks.

sentences.zh: 小生之詆，恐取辱於廬江；

translations.literal: A petty student's slander—I fear taking shame at Lujiang;
translations.idiomatic: Were I to send you the scribblings of a minor talent, I would fear the disgrace Ruan Ji brought upon himself at Lujiang;

sentences.zh: 遮道之姦，慮興謀於從事。

translations.literal: A villain blocking the road—I worry about plotting arising from the staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: and were I to waylay you with them, I would worry about provoking the sort of plot a staff officer might hatch.

sentences.zh: 方且褰帷自厲，求瘼不休，筆墨之功，曾何暇豫。

translations.literal: Just now I am lifting the curtain to exhort myself, seeking afflictions without rest; brush and ink achievements—how could there be leisure for them?
translations.idiomatic: For now I am raising the curtain of office to spur myself on, seeking out the people's woes without pause; how could I possibly find leisure for literary work?

sentences.zh: 至於心乎愛矣，未嘗有歇，思樂惠音，清風靡聞。

translations.literal: As for the heart that loves, there has never been rest; thinking of and delighting in gracious words, the clear breeze has never been heard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in my heart affection never ceases; I long to hear your gracious words, but no word from you has reached me.

sentences.zh: 譬夫夢想溫玉，饑渴明珠，雖愧卞、隨，猶爲好事。

translations.literal: It is like dreaming of warm jade, hungering and thirsting for bright pearls; although ashamed before Bian and Sui, it is still a good affair.
translations.idiomatic: It is like dreaming of warm jade or thirsting for a luminous pearl—though I cannot compare with Bian He or Sui He, I am still eager for such treasures.

sentences.zh: 新有所制，想能示之。

translations.literal: Newly there are compositions; I think you can show them.
translations.idiomatic: You must have written something new—surely you can share it with me.

sentences.zh: 勿等清慮，徒虛其請。

translations.literal: Do not wait for clear deliberation; vainly make the request empty.
translations.idiomatic: Do not keep me waiting while you deliberate; do not let my request come to nothing.

sentences.zh: 無由賞悉，遣此代懷。

translations.literal: Having no means to appreciate fully, I dispatch this in place of feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to convey my full appreciation, I send this letter to stand in for what is in my heart.

sentences.zh: 數路計行，遲還芳札。

translations.literal: Counting the routes and reckoning the journey, return late the fragrant letter.
translations.idiomatic: I reckon the distance by every road and await the late return of your gracious reply.

sentences.zh: 」孝綽答曰：「伏承自辭皇邑，爰至荊臺，未勞刺舉，且摛高麗。

translations.literal: " Xiaochuo replied: "I humbly learn that since you left the imperial capital, arriving at the Jing terrace, without troubling yourself with denunciation, you have moreover unfolded splendid beauty."
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaochuo replied: "I humbly hear that since you left the imperial capital for the Jingzhou post, without need of censure you have already produced work of rare brilliance."

sentences.zh: 近雖預觀尺錦，而不睹全玉。

translations.literal: Recently, although I have beforehand observed a foot of brocade, I have not seen the whole jade.
translations.idiomatic: Though I have lately glimpsed a fragment of your brocade, I have not yet seen the whole jade.

sentences.zh: 昔臨淄詞賦，悉與楊脩，未殫寶笥，顧慚先哲。

translations.literal: Formerly at Linzi the ci and fu—all were with Yang Xiu; the treasure coffer was not exhausted, yet I feel shame before the former sages.
translations.idiomatic: In old days at Linzi the prince's rhapsodies all went to Yang Xiu, yet that treasure chest was hardly emptied—I only feel shame when I think of those greater men of the past.

sentences.zh: 渚宮舊俗，朝衣多故，李固之薦二邦，徐珍之奏七邑，威懷之道，兼而有之。

translations.literal: Zhugong's old customs—court robes many with reasons; Li Gu's recommendation of two states, Xu Zhen's memorial on seven districts—the way of awe and cherishing, both possessed together.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhugong the old custom was that many court robes meant much to attend to—Li Gu recommended two commanderies and Xu Zhen reported on seven districts; your way combines both stern authority and gentle care.

sentences.zh: 當欲使金石流功，恥用翰墨垂迹。

translations.literal: You surely wish to make metal and stone transmit merit, ashamed to use brush and ink to leave traces.
translations.idiomatic: You surely wish your deeds to be inscribed in metal and stone, and are reluctant to win fame through mere letters.

sentences.zh: 雖乖知二，偶達聖心。

translations.literal: Although at odds with knowing two, by chance reaching the sage heart.
translations.idiomatic: Although I fall short of grasping your dual aims, by chance I have hit upon your noble purpose.

sentences.zh: 爰自退居素裏，卻掃窮閈，比楊倫之不出，譬張摯之杜門。

translations.literal: From the time of retiring to dwell in plain inner rooms, clearing away the broom at the poor doorway—comparing to Yang Lun's not going out, like Zhang Zhi's closing the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Since I withdrew to live simply behind closed doors, I have been like Yang Lun who never left home, like Zhang Zhi who barred his gate.

sentences.zh: 昔趙卿窮愁，肆言得失；

translations.literal: Formerly Master Zhao in desperate sorrow, freely spoke gains and losses;
translations.idiomatic: In old times Zhao Qi, crushed by adversity, wrote freely about right and wrong;

sentences.zh: 漢臣鬱志，廣敘盛衰。

translations.literal: Han minister with pent-up will, broadly narrated rise and decline.
translations.idiomatic: the Han minister Ban Gu, his ambitions thwarted, wrote at length of dynastic rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 彼此一時，擬非其匹。

translations.literal: Each other one time, comparing not their match.
translations.idiomatic: They were men of another age; I am no fit comparison to them.

sentences.zh: 竊以文豹何辜，以文爲罪。

translations.literal: I privately think: what crime has the patterned leopard, that writing should be his crime?
translations.idiomatic: I fear the patterned leopard is blameless—yet writing has become my crime.

sentences.zh: 由此而談，又何容易。

translations.literal: From this speaking, again how easy?
translations.idiomatic: Speaking from this, how could it be easy?

sentences.zh: 故韜翰吮墨，多歷寒暑，旣闕子幼南山之歌，又微敬通渭水之賦，無以自同獻笑，少酬褒誘。

translations.literal: Therefore I sheathe brush and suck ink, passing many cold and hot seasons; already lacking Ziyou's song of the southern mountains, and slighted by Jingtong's Wei River fu—I have no means to compare myself to offering laughter, little to repay praise and enticement.
translations.idiomatic: So I have kept brush and ink hidden through many seasons; I lack both Liu Chen's "Southern Mountain" and Ban Gu's Wei River rhapsody—how could I compare with those who bring delight, or repay your praise and encouragement?

sentences.zh: 且才乖體物，不擬作於玄根；

translations.literal: Moreover talent at odds with embodying things, not intending to compose at the mysterious root;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover my talent ill suits descriptive composition; I dare not attempt works like Xuan Gen's;

sentences.zh: 事殊宿諾，寧貽懼於硃亥。

translations.literal: The matter differs from an old promise; would rather leave fear at Zhuhai.
translations.idiomatic: My case is not like an old pledge kept at all costs; I would rather not share the fate of Zhu Zhihai.

sentences.zh: 顧己反躬，載懷累息。

translations.literal: Looking at self, turning body inward, bearing on the heart repeated sighs.
translations.idiomatic: Looking inward upon myself, my heart is full of sigh upon sigh.

sentences.zh: 但瞻言漢廣，邈若天涯，區區一心，分宵九逝。

translations.literal: Only gazing at words from the broad Han, distant as heaven's edge, the small single heart divides the night into nine deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when I think of you the distance is like the far side of the Han River—though my heart is small, it crosses nine deaths in a single night.

sentences.zh: 殿下降情白屋，存問相尋，食椹懷音，矧伊人矣。」

translations.literal: Your Highness lowered sentiment to the white-thatched house, inquiries seeking each other; eating mulberry, cherishing sounds—how much more for that person!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has honored a humble dwelling with your affection and sent repeated inquiries; if even eating mulberries makes one remember a voice, how much more should I cherish you!"

sentences.zh: 孝綽免職後，高祖數使僕射徐勉宣旨慰撫之，每朝宴常引與焉。

translations.literal: After Xiaochuo's dismissal from office, Emperor Gaozu repeatedly sent Vice Director Xu Mian to convey imperial intent and comfort him; at every court banquet he was regularly invited to attend.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaochuo was dismissed, Emperor Gaozu repeatedly sent Vice Director Xu Mian with imperial messages of consolation, and at court banquets he was regularly invited to join the company.

sentences.zh: 及高祖爲《籍田詩》，又使勉先示孝綽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu composed the "Field-Cultivation Poem," he again had Mian show it first to Xiaochuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu wrote the "Field-Cultivation Poem," he again had Mian show the draft to Xiaochuo first.

sentences.zh: 時奉詔作者數十人，高祖以孝綽尤工，卽日有敕，起爲西中郎湘東王諮議。

translations.literal: At the time dozens composed on imperial command; Emperor Gaozu considered Xiaochuo especially skilled, and that same day issued an edict restoring him as Consultant to the Prince of Xiangdong, Western Palace Lieutenant.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens were then composing on imperial command; Emperor Gaozu judged Xiaochuo the finest craftsman, and that very day issued an edict restoring him as Consultant to the Prince of Xiangdong, Western Palace Lieutenant.

sentences.zh: 啓謝曰：「臣不能銜珠避顛，傾柯衛足，以茲疏幸，與物多忤。

translations.literal: He memorialized in thanks, saying: "Your servant cannot hold a pearl to avoid disaster or tilt the branch to protect his feet; because of this frank good fortune, I often clash with others."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized his thanks: "Your servant cannot hold a pearl to ward off calamity or tilt the branch to shelter his feet; because of this blunt good fortune, I have often clashed with others."

sentences.zh: 兼逢匿怨之友，遂居司隸之官，交構是非，用成萋斐。

translations.literal: Moreover I encountered friends nursing hidden resentment; I then held the Censorate office, fabricating right and wrong, thereby producing tangled slander.
translations.idiomatic: I also fell in with friends who nursed hidden grudges; when I held the Censorate post, they twisted truth and falsehood until slander took root.

sentences.zh: 日月昭回，俯明枉直。

translations.literal: Sun and moon revolve clearly; looking down, wrong and right are illumined.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon wheel through the sky, and from above wrong and right are made plain.

sentences.zh: 獄書每御，輒鑒蔣濟之冤；

translations.literal: Each time prison documents reached the throne, Your Majesty discerned Jiang Ji's injustice;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever prison reports reached the throne, Your Majesty saw through the injustice done to Jiang Ji;

sentences.zh: 炙發見明，非關陳正之辯。

translations.literal: Burning hair revealed innocence—not owing to Chen Zheng's argument.
translations.idiomatic: innocence was proved by burning hair—not through Chen Zheng's eloquence.

sentences.zh: 遂漏斯密網，免彼嚴棘，得使還同士伍，比屋唐民，生死肉骨，豈侔其施。

translations.literal: Thus slipping through the fine net, escaping those harsh thorns, I was able to return as one among common ranks, neighbor to Tang's people—bringing the dead to life and flesh to bone; how could my case compare with such grace?
translations.idiomatic: Thus I slipped through the fine net and escaped harsh punishment, returning to live among common soldiers like neighbors in the age of Tang—restoring life to the dead and flesh to bone; how could such grace be matched?

sentences.zh: 臣誠無識，孰不戴天。

translations.literal: Your servant truly lacks understanding—who would not bear heaven on his head?
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is truly without understanding—who would not feel bound to Heaven for such mercy?

sentences.zh: 疏遠畝隴，絕望高闕，而降其接引，優以旨喻，於臣微物，足爲榮隕。

translations.literal: Far from furrows and fields, despairing of the high palace—yet Your Majesty lowered yourself to guide me and favored me with gracious counsel; for this petty creature it is glory enough to die for.
translations.idiomatic: Though I was far from the fields and had despaired of the high palace, Your Majesty lowered yourself to guide me and favored me with gracious counsel—for this petty creature, that alone would be honor enough to die for.

sentences.zh: 況剛條落葉，忽沾雲露；

translations.literal: How much more when rigid branches shed leaves, suddenly touched by cloud and dew;
translations.idiomatic: How much more when stiff branches that had shed their leaves suddenly receive cloud and dew;

sentences.zh: 周行所置，復齒盛流。

translations.literal: Among the array of offices, again taking rank among the great stream.
translations.idiomatic: among the ranks of office I again take my place among the great and flourishing.

sentences.zh: 但雕朽杇糞，徒成延獎；

translations.literal: But carving rotten wood and plastering with dung—vainly earning extended praise;
translations.idiomatic: But I am rotten wood smeared with dung—any extended praise is wasted on me;

sentences.zh: 捕影系風，終無效答。

translations.literal: Chasing shadows and tethering wind—in the end no effective reply.
translations.idiomatic: chasing shadows and tethering wind—in the end I can offer no worthy reply.

sentences.zh: 」又啓謝東宮曰：「臣聞之，先聖以『衆惡之，必察焉；

translations.literal: " Again he memorialized in thanks to the Eastern Palace, saying: "Your servant has heard that the ancient sages said, 'When the multitude hates someone, examine him;
translations.idiomatic: " He also memorialized his thanks to the Eastern Palace: "Your servant has heard the ancient sages say, 'When the multitude hates a man, examine him;

sentences.zh: 衆好之，必察焉』。

translations.literal: when the multitude loves someone, examine him.'"
translations.idiomatic: when the multitude loves a man, examine him.'"

sentences.zh: 豈非孤特則積毀所歸，比周則積譽斯信？

translations.literal: Is it not that standing alone draws accumulated slander, while clustering together draws accumulated praise?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not that standing alone draws accumulated slander, while banding together wins accumulated praise?

sentences.zh: 知好惡之間，必待明鑒。

translations.literal: Between knowing like and dislike, clear judgment must be awaited.
translations.idiomatic: Between liking and disliking, clear judgment is indispensable.

sentences.zh: 故晏嬰再爲阿宰，而前毀後譽。

translations.literal: Therefore Yan Ying twice served as steward of a small town, and had slander before and praise after.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Yan Ying, twice magistrate of a small town, was slandered at first and praised afterward.

sentences.zh: 後譽出於阿意，前毀由於直道。

translations.literal: Later praise arose from agreeable intent; earlier slander arose from the straight path.
translations.idiomatic: Later praise came from pleasing others; earlier slander came from walking the straight path.

sentences.zh: 是以一犬所噬，旨酒貿其甘酸；

translations.literal: Thus one dog's bite can trade away the sweetness and sourness of fine wine;
translations.idiomatic: Thus one dog's bite can spoil the sweetness and sourness of fine wine;

sentences.zh: 一手所搖，嘉樹變其生死。

translations.literal: One hand's shake can change a fine tree's life and death.
translations.idiomatic: one hand's shake can decide whether a fine tree lives or dies.

sentences.zh: 又鄒陽有言，士無賢愚，入朝見嫉。

translations.literal: Moreover Zou Yang said: scholar, whether worthy or foolish, upon entering court meets jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yang also said that whether a scholar is worthy or foolish, once he enters court he meets jealousy.

sentences.zh: 至若臧文之下展季，靳尚之放靈均，絳侯之排賈生，平津之陷主父，自茲厥後，其徒實繁。

translations.literal: As when Zang Wen drove down Zhan Ji, Jin Shang banished Ling Jun, the Marquis of Jiang excluded Jia Yi, Pingjin trapped Zhufu—since then their kind has truly been numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Think of Zang Wen driving down Huiliu Ji, Jin Shang banishing Qu Yuan, the Marquis of Jiang excluding Jia Yi, and Gongsun Hong trapping Zhufu Yan—since then their kind has been truly numerous.

sentences.zh: 曲筆短辭，不暇殫述，寸管所窺，常由切齒。

translations.literal: With bent brush and brief words, I lack time to exhaust the telling; what this inch of brush glimpses often makes one gnash teeth.
translations.idiomatic: With a bent brush and brief words I cannot tell the whole story; what this inch of brush has glimpsed often makes me gnash my teeth.

sentences.zh: 殿下誨道觀書，俯同好學，前載枉直，備該神覽。

translations.literal: Your Highness instructs in the Way and reads books, bowing to the same love of learning; past records of wrong and right are fully grasped in your divine reading.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness teaches the Way and reads widely, sharing the love of learning; past records of wrong and right are fully comprehended in your clear sight.

sentences.zh: 臣昔因立侍，親承緒言，飄風貝錦，譬彼讒慝，聖旨殷勤，深以爲歎。

translations.literal: Your servant once stood in attendance and personally received Your Highness's continuing words: 'A wind blows; brocade patterns'—like slander and evil; the sacred intent was earnest and deeply sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant once stood in attendance and heard Your Highness's own words on how 'the wind blows and brocade patterns appear'—a likeness of slander and malice; the earnest imperial intent moved me deeply.

sentences.zh: 臣資愚履直，不能杜漸防微，曾未幾何，逢訧罹難。

translations.literal: Your servant's nature is foolish yet treads straight; I could not stop the gradual and guard the subtle—before long I met conflict and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is foolish by nature yet walks a straight path; I could not stop trouble at its first stir—before long I met conflict and disaster.

sentences.zh: 雖吹毛洗垢，在朝而同嗟；

translations.literal: Although picking at hairs and washing stains, the court alike sighed;
translations.idiomatic: Though the court picked at hairs and washed stains and sighed together;

sentences.zh: 而嚴文峻法，肆姦其必奏。

translations.literal: Yet strict documents and harsh law—those who indulge evil must be reported.
translations.idiomatic: strict documents and harsh law still required that those who indulged evil be reported.

sentences.zh: 不顧賣友，志欲要君，自非上帝運超己之光，昭陵陽之虐，舞文虛謗，不取信於宸明，在縲嬰纆，幸得蠲於庸暗。

translations.literal: Disregarding selling friends, intent wishing to corner the lord—had not Heaven's Lord moved beyond self's light, exposed the tyranny of Zhao Yang, woven empty slander in legal documents, failed to win faith from imperial brilliance—in bonds and fetters, by fortune I was released from mediocre blindness.
translations.idiomatic: They cared nothing for betraying friends and sought only to corner their lord—had Heaven's Lord not looked beyond himself, exposed Zhao Yang's cruelty, and seen through the empty slander woven into legal documents, I would have remained in bonds and fetters; by fortune I was spared by mediocre blindness.

sentences.zh: 裁下免黜之書，仍頒朝會之旨。

translations.literal: Just issued the dismissal edict, yet still issued the court audience decree.
translations.idiomatic: You had just issued the dismissal edict, yet still sent word summoning me to court.

sentences.zh: 小人未識通方，縶馬懸車，息絕朝覲。

translations.literal: This petty man did not know flexibility; I hitched my horse and hung up my carriage, ceasing court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: This petty man did not know how to adapt; I hitched my horse and hung up my carriage and ceased attending court.

sentences.zh: 方願滅影銷聲，遂移林穀。

translations.literal: I then wished to erase shadow and silence voice, to move into forest and valley.
translations.idiomatic: I then wished to vanish without trace and retire to forest and valley.

sentences.zh: 不悟天聽罔已，造次必彰，不以距違見疵，復使引籍雲陛。

translations.literal: I did not realize Heaven's hearing is never absent; haste must show itself—you did not fault me for refusal, but again had me enter the registry at the cloud steps.
translations.idiomatic: I did not realize Heaven's ear is never absent and that haste always shows itself—you did not fault me for refusing, but again had my name entered at the cloud steps of court.

sentences.zh: 降寬和之色，垂布帛之言，形之千載，所蒙已厚；

translations.literal: You lowered a generous and harmonious countenance, bestowed words like cloth and silk—inscribed for a thousand ages, the grace received is already thick;
translations.idiomatic: You showed a generous and harmonious countenance and bestowed words gentle as cloth and silk—grace to be recorded for a thousand ages, already more than I deserve;

sentences.zh: 況乃恩等特召，榮同起家，望古自惟，彌覺多忝。

translations.literal: How much more when the favor equals a special summons, glory equals beginning from family rank—looking to antiquity and examining myself, I feel only more unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the favor equals a special summons and the glory equals rising from humble beginnings—looking to antiquity and examining myself, I feel only more unworthy.

sentences.zh: 但未渝丹石，永藏輪軌，相彼工言，構茲媒諓。

translations.literal: But though my cinnabar heart is unchanged and forever hidden in wheel-tracks, those skilled in words weave this matchmaking slander.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though my loyal heart is unchanged and forever hidden in wheel-tracks, those skilled in words weave this slander against me.

sentences.zh: 且款冬而生，已凋柯葉，空延德澤，無謝陽春。」

translations.literal: Moreover, flowering in winter, branches and leaves already withered—I vainly receive virtue's dew, unable to repay the spring sun."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I am like a plant that blooms in winter, its branches and leaves already withered—I vainly receive your virtue's dew and cannot repay the spring sun."

sentences.zh: 後爲太子僕，母憂去職。

translations.literal: Later he was made Crown Prince Steward; on his mother's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Crown Prince Steward; when his mother died he left office to mourn.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除安西湘東王諮議參軍，遷黃門侍郎，尚書吏部郎，坐受人絹一束，爲餉者所訟，左遷信威臨賀王長史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed Consultative Officer of the Prince of Xiangdong, General Who Pacifies the West; promoted to Palace Attendant, then Director of the Personnel Section in the Ministry of Works; for accepting a bundle of silk he was impeached by the giver and demoted to Chief Secretary to the Prince of Linhe, Prince of Xixin.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed Consultative Officer on the staff of the Prince of Xiangdong, General Who Pacifies the West; he was promoted to Palace Attendant and then Director of the Personnel Section, but for accepting a bundle of silk he was impeached by the donor and demoted to Chief Secretary to the Prince of Linhe, Prince of Xixin.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷秘書監。

translations.literal: Before long, he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大同五年，卒官，時年五十九。

translations.literal: In Datong year 5 he died in office, aged fifty-nine at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Datong he died in office, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 孝綽少有盛名，而仗氣負才，多所陵忽，有不合意，極言詆訾。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo early had great fame, but relied on spirit and prided himself on talent, often looking down on others; when displeased he spoke slander in extreme terms.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo won great fame early, but he relied on his spirit and pride in his talent, often looking down on others; when displeased he spoke in the harshest terms of slander.

sentences.zh: 領軍臧盾、太府卿沈僧杲等，並被時遇，孝綽尤輕之。

translations.literal: General-in-Chief Zang Dun, Grand Storekeeper Shen Senggao, and others all enjoyed the favor of the age; Xiaochuo especially looked down on them.
translations.idiomatic: General-in-Chief Zang Dun, Grand Storekeeper Shen Senggao, and others all enjoyed the favor of the times, but Xiaochuo especially looked down on them.

sentences.zh: 每於朝集會同處，公卿間無所與語，反呼騶卒訪道途間事，由此多忤於物。

translations.literal: At every court assembly when gathered together, among ministers he spoke with no one, but instead called grooms to ask about road matters—thereby often clashing with people.
translations.idiomatic: At every court assembly he spoke with none of the ministers, but instead called grooms over to ask about road conditions—thereby often offending people.

sentences.zh: 孝綽辭藻爲後進所宗，世重其文，每作一篇，朝成暮遍，好事者咸諷誦傳寫，流聞絕域。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo's literary style was revered by later generations; the world prized his writings; each piece, finished in the morning, circulated by evening; enthusiasts all recited and copied them, spreading to distant lands.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo's literary style was revered by the younger generation; the world prized his writings, and each piece finished in the morning circulated by evening; enthusiasts recited and copied them until they spread to distant lands.

sentences.zh: 文集數十萬言，行於世。

translations.literal: His collected works number several hundred thousand words and circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works run to several hundred thousand words and circulate widely.

sentences.zh: 孝綽兄弟及羣從諸子侄，當時有七十人，並能屬文，近古未之有也。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo's brothers and all the sons and nephews of his clan numbered seventy at the time, all able to compose writing—unprecedented in recent antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo's brothers and all the sons and nephews of his clan numbered seventy at the time, all able to compose writing—unprecedented in recent times.

sentences.zh: 其三妹適琅邪王叔英、吳郡張嵊、東海徐悱，並有才學；

translations.literal: His three younger sisters married Wang Shuying of Langya, Zhang Sheng of Wu commandery, and Xu Ti of Donghai—all possessed literary talent;
translations.idiomatic: His three younger sisters married Wang Shuying of Langya, Zhang Sheng of Wu commandery, and Xu Ti of Donghai—all were accomplished in letters;

sentences.zh: 悱妻文尤清拔。

translations.literal: Xu's wife's writing was especially pure and striking.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ti's wife wrote with especial clarity and force.

sentences.zh: 悱，僕射徐勉子，爲晉安郡，卒，喪還京師，妻爲祭文，辭甚悽愴。

translations.literal: Xu Ti, son of Vice Director Xu Mian, served as prefect of Jin'an; he died; when the coffin returned to the capital his wife composed a sacrificial text, the wording extremely mournful.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ti, son of Vice Director Xu Mian, served as prefect of Jin'an; when he died and his coffin returned to the capital, his wife composed a sacrificial text of extraordinary pathos.

sentences.zh: 勉本欲爲哀文，旣睹此文，於是閣筆。

translations.literal: Mian had originally intended to write a lament; once he saw this text, he thereupon put down his brush.
translations.idiomatic: Mian had originally intended to write a lament himself, but once he read this text he put down his brush.

sentences.zh: 孝綽子諒，字求信。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo's son Liang, style-name Qiuxin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo's son Liang, courtesy name Qiuxin.

sentences.zh: 少好學，有文才，尤博悉晉代故事，時人號曰「皮裏晉書」。

translations.literal: From youth fond of learning, possessing literary talent, especially thoroughly knowing Jin-dynasty anecdotes; people of the time called him "the Jin History in a skin wrapper."
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and had literary talent; he was especially steeped in Jin-dynasty anecdotes, and people of the time called him "the Jin History in a skin wrapper."

sentences.zh: 歷官著作佐郎，太子舍人，王府主簿，功曹史，中城王記室參軍。

translations.literal: His offices passed through Assistant Gentleman of the Compilation Bureau, Crown Prince Attendant, prince's household chief clerk, merit officer, and recorder-attendant to the Prince of Zhongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Assistant Gentleman of the Compilation Bureau, Crown Prince Attendant, prince's household chief clerk, merit officer, and recorder-attendant to the Prince of Zhongcheng.

sentences.zh: 王筠字元禮，一字德柔，琅邪臨沂人。

translations.literal: Wang Yun, courtesy name Yuanli, alternate courtesy name Derou, a native of Linyi in Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun, courtesy name Yuanli and also styled Derou, was a native of Linyi in Langya.

sentences.zh: 祖僧虔，齊司空簡穆公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sengqian was Qi Minister of Works, Duke Jianmu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengqian was Duke Jianmu, Minister of Works of Qi.

sentences.zh: 父楫，太中大夫。

translations.literal: His father Ji, Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji served as Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 筠幼警寤，七歲能屬文。

translations.literal: Yun from youth was quick-witted; at seven he could compose writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was precocious from childhood; at seven he could already compose writing.

sentences.zh: 年十六，爲《芍藥賦》，甚美。

translations.literal: At age sixteen he composed "Peony Fu," very beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he wrote "Peony Fu," a work of great beauty.

sentences.zh: 及長，清靜好學，與從兄泰齊名。

translations.literal: When grown, quiet and fond of learning, he was equally famous with his cousin Tai.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he was quiet and fond of learning, and was equally famous with his cousin Tai.

sentences.zh: 陳郡謝覽，覽弟舉，亦有重譽，時人爲之語曰：「謝有覽舉，王有養炬。

translations.literal: Xie Lan of Chen commandery and Lan's younger brother Ju also had great repute; people of the time made a saying: "The Xies have Lan and Ju; the Wangs have Yang and Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lan of Chen commandery and his younger brother Ju also enjoyed great repute, and people of the time said: "The Xies have Lan and Ju; the Wangs have Yang and Ju.

sentences.zh: 」炬是泰，養卽筠，並小字也。

translations.literal: " Ju refers to Tai; Yang refers to Yun—they are both childhood names.
translations.idiomatic: " Ju was Tai's childhood name and Yang was Yun's—they were both pet names.

sentences.zh: 起家中軍臨川王行參軍，遷太子舍人，除尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as Acting Aide on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan, Central Army Commander; transferred to Crown Prince Attendant; appointed Director of the Palace Section in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Acting Aide on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan, Central Army Commander; he was transferred to Crown Prince Attendant and then appointed Director of the Palace Section in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 王氏過江以來，未有居郎署者，或勸逡巡不就，筠曰：「陸平原東南之秀，王文度獨步江東，吾得比蹤昔人，何所多恨。

translations.literal: Since the Wang clan crossed the river, none had held a Secretariat post; some advised hesitation and not accepting; Yun said: "Lu Pingyuan was the southeast's finest; Wang Wendu walked alone in Jiangdong—I can compare my footsteps to men of old, what is there much to regret?
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wang clan crossed the Yangzi, none had held a Secretariat post; some urged him to hesitate and decline; Yun said: "Lu Ji was the finest talent of the southeast; Wang Huizhi walked alone in Jiangdong—I may compare my footsteps with men of old; what is there to regret?

sentences.zh: 」乃欣然就職。

translations.literal: " Thereupon with glad heart he took up the office.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he gladly took up the post.

sentences.zh: 尚書令沈約，當世辭宗，每見筠文，咨嗟吟詠，以爲不逮也。

translations.literal: Director Shen Yue, literary patriarch of the age, whenever he saw Yun's writings would sigh in admiration and chant them, thinking himself not equal.
translations.idiomatic: Director Shen Yue, the literary patriarch of the age, whenever he saw Yun's writings would sigh in admiration and chant them aloud, thinking himself not Yun's equal.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂筠：「昔蔡伯喈見王仲宣稱曰：『王公之孫也，吾家書籍，悉當相與。

translations.literal: Once he said to Yun: "Formerly Cai Yong saw Wang Can and said: 'He is a grandson of the Wang clan; all the books in my house shall be shared with him.'
translations.idiomatic: Once he said to Yun: "When Cai Yong met Wang Can he said: 'He is a grandson of the Wang house; all the books in my home shall be shared with him.'

sentences.zh: 』僕雖不敏，請附斯言。

translations.literal: " Though I am not sharp, I ask to attach myself to those words.
translations.idiomatic: " Though I am not clever, I ask to attach myself to those words.

sentences.zh: 自謝朓諸賢零落已後，平生意好，殆將都絕，不謂疲暮，復逢於君。

translations.literal: Since Xie Tiao and the other worthies passed away, the friends of my life's heart are nearly all gone—I did not expect in weary old age to meet you again.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xie Tiao and the other worthies passed away, the friends of my heart are nearly all gone; I did not expect, in weary old age, to meet you again.

sentences.zh: 」約於郊居宅造閣齋，筠爲草木十詠，書之於壁，皆直寫文詞，不加篇題。

translations.literal: " Yue built a pavilion study at his suburban residence; Yun made Ten Odes on Plants and wrote them on the walls, all directly writing the text without adding titles.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue built a pavilion study at his suburban residence; Yun composed Ten Odes on Plants and wrote them on the walls, copying the text directly without adding titles.

sentences.zh: 約謂人云：「此詩指物呈形，無假題署。

translations.literal: Yue told people: "These poems present things in their form without needing titles.
translations.idiomatic: Yue told people: "These poems present things in their own form without needing titles.

sentences.zh: 」約制《郊居賦》，構思積時，猶未都畢，乃要筠示其草，筠讀至「雌霓連蜷」，約撫掌欣抃曰：「僕嘗恐人呼爲霓。

translations.literal: " Yue was composing "Suburban Residence Fu"; accumulating ideas for a long time, it was still not all finished; he therefore asked Yun to show the draft; when Yun read to "the female rainbow coiled," Yue clapped his hands in delight and said: "I once feared people would call it ni (rainbow secondary).
translations.idiomatic: " Yue was composing "Suburban Residence Fu"; he had been accumulating ideas for a long time and it was still unfinished, so he asked Yun to show him the draft; when Yun read to "the female rainbow coiled," Yue clapped his hands in delight and said: "I once feared people would read it as ni.

sentences.zh: 」次至「墜石磓星」，及「冰懸坎而帶坻」。

translations.literal: " Next to "fallen stones pounding stars" and "ice hanging in the pit and girding the islet."
translations.idiomatic: " Then to "fallen stones pounding stars" and "ice hanging in the pit and girding the islet."

sentences.zh: 筠皆擊節稱讚。

translations.literal: Yun each time beat the measure and praised.
translations.idiomatic: Yun beat time with his hand and praised each passage.

sentences.zh: 約曰：「知音者希，真賞殆絕，所以相要，政在此數句耳。

translations.literal: Yue said: "Those who understand music are rare; true appreciation is nearly extinct—therefore I invited you, precisely for these few lines."
translations.idiomatic: Yue said: "Connoisseurs are few and true appreciation nearly gone—that is why I asked you here, for these few lines alone."

sentences.zh: 」筠又嘗爲詩呈約，卽報書云：「覽所示詩，實爲麗則，聲和被紙，光影盈字。

translations.literal: " Yun again once presented a poem to Yue, who immediately replied in a letter: "Having read the poem you showed me, it is truly beautiful and correct; sounds harmonize against the paper, light and brilliance fill the characters."
translations.idiomatic: " Yun once sent Yue a poem; Yue replied at once: "Reading the poem you showed me, I find it truly beautiful and correct—its harmonies ring against the page and light seems to spill from every character."

sentences.zh: 夔、牙接響，顧有餘慚；

translations.literal: Kui and Ya answer in echo—yet I have surplus shame;
translations.idiomatic: Like Kui and Boya echoing in reply, I still feel more shame than pride;

sentences.zh: 孔翠羣翔，豈不多愧。

translations.literal: Peacocks and kingfishers flock in flight—how could I not feel much shame?
translations.idiomatic: When peacocks and kingfishers flock together in flight, how could I not feel deeply ashamed?

sentences.zh: 古情拙目，每佇新奇，爛然總至，權輿已盡。

translations.literal: Old feelings dull the eye; each time I await novelty—splendid brilliance all arrives; the carriage has already reached its end.
translations.idiomatic: Old habit dulls the eye, yet each time I wait for something new, splendor arrives in full—until even the first stirrings are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 會昌昭發，蘭揮玉振，克諧之義，寧比笙簧。

translations.literal: Meeting brilliance and manifest splendor, orchid-waving and jade-vibrating—the meaning of perfect harmony—how could it compare to pipes and reeds?
translations.idiomatic: Brilliance meets and shines forth; orchids sway and jade chimes ring—such perfect harmony cannot be compared with mere pipes and reeds.

sentences.zh: 思力所該，一至乎此，嘆服吟研，周流忘念。

translations.literal: The range of thought and power reaches this point; sighing in admiration, chanting and studying, flowing all around, forgetting other thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: The reach of your thought and power extends to this height; I sigh in admiration, chant and study your lines, and lose myself in them entirely.

sentences.zh: 昔時幼壯，頗愛斯文，含咀之間，倏焉疲暮。

translations.literal: In former days in youth and prime, I quite loved this literature; in the interval of savoring, suddenly weary old age came.
translations.idiomatic: In my youth and prime I loved this kind of writing; but while I was still savoring it, old age came upon me all at once.

sentences.zh: 不及後進，誠非一人，擅美推能，實歸吾子。

translations.literal: Not matching the later generation is truly not only one person; monopolizing beauty and recommending talent actually belongs to you, my lord.
translations.idiomatic: That I cannot match the younger generation is not mine alone to say; to monopolize beauty and recommend talent truly belongs to you, my lord.

sentences.zh: 遲比閑日，清覯乃申。

translations.literal: Delayed to compare on leisure days; a clear meeting shall then be extended.
translations.idiomatic: Let us wait for a free day, and then meet face to face at leisure.

sentences.zh: 」筠爲文能壓強韻，每公宴並作，辭必妍美。

translations.literal: " Yun in composing could overcome strong rhyme constraints; at each public banquet when composing together, his wording was invariably beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: " Yun could compose even under the hardest rhyme schemes; at every public banquet where they wrote together, his language was invariably beautiful.

sentences.zh: 約常從容啓高祖曰：「晚來名家，唯見王筠獨步。」

translations.literal: Yue often calmly memorialized Emperor Gaozu, saying: "Among late-coming famous clans, I see only Wang Yun walking alone."
translations.idiomatic: Yue often said calmly to Emperor Gaozu: "Among the great literary houses of recent times, I see only Wang Yun standing alone."

sentences.zh: 累遷太子洗馬，中舍人，並掌東宮管記。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Crown Prince Groom, Palace Attendant, and concurrently managed Eastern Palace records.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Crown Prince Groom and Palace Attendant, and concurrently managed the Eastern Palace records.

sentences.zh: 昭明太子愛文學士，常與筠及劉孝綽、陸倕、到洽、殷芸等游宴玄圃，太子獨執筠袖撫孝綽肩而言曰：「所謂左把浮丘袖，右拍洪崖肩。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhaoming loved literary scholars; he often feasted and wandered in the Mystic Garden with Yun and Liu Xiaochuo, Lu Chi, Dao Qia, Yin Yun, and others; the Crown Prince alone grasped Yun's sleeve and patted Xiaochuo's shoulder, saying: "This is what is called: 'Left hand grasping Fuqiu's sleeve, right hand patting Hongya's shoulder.'
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhaoming loved literary scholars and often feasted with Yun, Liu Xiaochuo, Lu Chi, Dao Qia, Yin Yun, and others in the Mystic Garden; the Crown Prince alone took Yun by the sleeve and Xiaochuo by the shoulder and said: "This is what people mean by 'grasping Fuqiu's sleeve with the left hand and patting Hongya's shoulder with the right.'

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: " He was valued this highly.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 筠又與殷芸以方雅見禮焉。

translations.literal: Yun, together with Yin Yun, was also received with courtesy for their refined correctness.
translations.idiomatic: Yun and Yin Yun were also honored for their refined and upright bearing.

sentences.zh: 出爲丹陽尹丞、北中郎諮議參軍，遷中書郎。

translations.literal: He went out as Assistant Magistrate of Danyang, Consultation Aide under the Northern General of the Guard, and was transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He served outside the capital as Assistant Magistrate of Danyang and Consultation Aide on the staff of the Northern General of the Guard, then was transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 奉敕制《開善寺寶誌大師碑文》，詞甚麗逸。

translations.literal: By imperial command he composed the "Memorial Stele Inscription for Master Baozhi of Kaishan Temple"; the wording was very beautiful and unfettered.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command he composed the memorial stele inscription for Master Baozhi of Kaishan Temple, in language of exceptional beauty and grace.

sentences.zh: 又敕撰《中書表奏》三十卷，及所上賦頌，都爲一集。

translations.literal: He was also by edict to compile Memorials and Petitions of the Secretariat in thirty volumes, together with submitted fu and hymns, all made into one collection.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to compile thirty volumes of Secretariat memorials and petitions, together with the fu and hymns he had submitted, all gathered into one collection.

sentences.zh: 俄兼寧遠湘東王長史，行府、國、郡事。

translations.literal: Soon he concurrently became Chief Administrator to the Prince of Xiangdong, General of Ningyuan, handling palace, state, and commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made Chief Administrator to the Prince of Xiangdong, General of Ningyuan, and handled the affairs of the princely establishment, fief, and commandery.

sentences.zh: 除太子家令，復掌管記。

translations.literal: Appointed Crown Prince Household Commandant; again managed records.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Crown Prince Household Commandant and again took charge of the records.

sentences.zh: 普通元年，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putong, he left office on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Putong he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 筠有孝性，毀瘠過禮，服闋後，疾廢久之。

translations.literal: Yun had a filial nature; his emaciation exceeded ritual propriety; after the mourning period ended, illness lingered for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was deeply filial; his grief emaciated him beyond what ritual required, and after the mourning period ended he remained ill and incapacitated for a long time.

sentences.zh: 六年，除尚書吏部郎，遷太子中庶子，領羽林監，又改領步兵。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Director of Personnel in the Ministry of Works; transferred to Crown Prince Household Vice-Administrator; headed the Palace Guard Directorate; then changed to head the Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed Director of Personnel in the Ministry of Works, then transferred to Crown Prince Household Vice-Administrator; he headed the Palace Guard Directorate and later the Footsoldiers as well.

sentences.zh: 中大通二年，遷司徒左長史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong, he was transferred to Left Chief Administrator of the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongdatong he was transferred to Left Chief Administrator of the Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 三年，昭明太子薨，敕爲哀策文，復見嗟賞。

translations.literal: In the third year Crown Prince Zhaoming died; by edict Yun composed the lament eulogy and again met sighing admiration.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Crown Prince Zhaoming died; by edict Yun composed the lament eulogy and was once again admired with sighs of praise.

sentences.zh: 尋出爲貞威將軍、臨海太守，在郡被訟，不調累年。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as General of Upright Might and Prefect of Linhai; in the commandery he faced lawsuits and was unresponsive for many years.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as General of Upright Might and Prefect of Linhai; lawsuits were brought against him in the commandery, and for many years he did not respond to summons.

sentences.zh: 大同初，起爲雲麾豫章王長史，遷秘書監。

translations.literal: Early in Datong he was recalled as Chief Administrator to the Prince of Yuzhang, Cloud-Banner General; transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Datong he was recalled as Chief Administrator to the Prince of Yuzhang, Cloud-Banner General, and then transferred to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五年，除太府卿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Minister Steward.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Minister Steward.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷度支尚書。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 中大同元年，出爲明威將軍、永嘉太守，以疾固辭，徙爲光祿大夫，俄遷雲騎將軍、司徒左長史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongdatong he went out as Bright Might General and Prefect of Yongjia; due to illness he firmly declined; he was moved to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; soon transferred to Cloud Cavalry General and Left Chief Administrator of the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongdatong he was sent out as Bright Might General and Prefect of Yongjia, but firmly declined on grounds of illness; he was reassigned as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and soon transferred to Cloud Cavalry General and Left Chief Administrator of the Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，侯景寇逼，筠時不入城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing pressed in attack; Yun at the time did not enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiqing, when Hou Jing pressed his attack, Yun did not enter the city.

sentences.zh: 明年，太宗卽位，爲太子詹事。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Taizong took the throne and made him Crown Prince Household Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when Emperor Taizong took the throne, Yun was made Crown Prince Household Mentor.

sentences.zh: 筠舊宅先爲賊所焚，乃寓居國子祭酒蕭子雲宅，夜忽有盜攻之，驚懼墜井卒，時年六十九。

translations.literal: Yun's old residence had first been burned by bandits; he therefore lodged in the home of Director of the Imperial University Xiao Ziyun; at night robbers suddenly attacked; in fright and fear he fell into a well and died; he was then sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's old residence had already been burned by bandits, so he lodged in the home of Xiao Ziyun, Director of the Imperial University; robbers attacked one night, and in terror he fell into a well and died at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 家人十餘人同遇害。

translations.literal: More than ten family members likewise met harm.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten members of his household were killed as well.

sentences.zh: 筠狀貌寢小，長不滿六尺。

translations.literal: Yun's appearance was small and slight; his height did not reach six chi.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was slight in build and stood less than six chi tall.

sentences.zh: 性弘厚，不以藝能高人，而少擅才名，與劉孝綽見重當世。

translations.literal: His nature was generous and thick; he did not use artistic talent to look down on others; yet from youth he excelled in talent and fame, and with Liu Xiaochuo was valued in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous by nature and never looked down on others because of his literary gifts, yet from youth he excelled in talent and fame and, together with Liu Xiaochuo, was highly regarded in his time.

sentences.zh: 其自序曰：「餘少好書，老而彌篤。

translations.literal: His self-preface says: "From youth I loved books; in old age I am all the more devoted."
translations.idiomatic: In his self-preface he wrote: "From youth I loved books, and in old age my devotion has only deepened."

sentences.zh: 雖偶見瞥觀，皆卽疏記，後重省覽，歡興彌深，習與性成，不覺筆倦。

translations.literal: Even when I chanced to glance briefly, I at once made brief notes; later when I reviewed them again, delight grew deeper; habit and nature formed together, and I did not notice weariness of the brush.
translations.idiomatic: Even when I only glanced at something in passing, I would jot it down at once; when I read those notes again later, my pleasure only deepened—habit had become second nature, and I never noticed my hand growing tired.

sentences.zh: 自年十三四，齊建武二年乙亥至梁大同六年，四十載矣。

translations.literal: From age thirteen or fourteen, from the yihai year, second year of Jianwu of Qi, to the sixth year of Datong of Liang—forty years.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of thirteen or fourteen, from the yihai year, the second year of Jianwu under Qi, to the sixth year of Datong under Liang—that is forty years.

sentences.zh: 幼年讀《五經》，皆七八十遍。

translations.literal: In childhood I read the Five Classics, each seven or eight tens of times.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood I read each of the Five Classics seventy or eighty times.

sentences.zh: 愛《左氏春秋》，吟諷常爲口實，廣略去取，凡三過五抄。

translations.literal: I loved the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals; chanting and reciting it was often on my lips; selecting broadly and narrowly, omitting and taking, altogether three times through and five copies.
translations.idiomatic: I loved the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals and often recited it aloud; I made abridged and expanded selections from it, reading it through three times and copying it five times.

sentences.zh: 餘經及《周官》、《儀禮》、《國語》、《爾雅》、《山海經》、《本草》並再抄。

translations.literal: The remaining classics and the Rites of Zhou, Ceremonial Rites, Discourses of the States, Erya, Classic of Mountains and Seas, and Materia Medica were each copied twice.
translations.idiomatic: The other classics, together with the Rites of Zhou, Ceremonial Rites, Discourses of the States, Erya, Classic of Mountains and Seas, and Materia Medica, I copied twice each.

sentences.zh: 子史諸集皆一遍。

translations.literal: Histories, masters, and various collected works—each once through.
translations.idiomatic: Histories, philosophical works, and collected writings I read once each.

sentences.zh: 未嘗倩人假手，並躬自抄錄，大小百餘卷。

translations.literal: I never asked others to lend a hand; all were personally copied and recorded, large and small, more than a hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: I never asked anyone else to copy for me; I copied everything myself, more than a hundred scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 不足傳之好事，蓋以備遺忘而已。

translations.literal: Not sufficient to pass on to lovers of such things—merely to guard against forgetting.
translations.idiomatic: These copies are not worth passing on to collectors; I made them only to guard against forgetting.

sentences.zh: 」又與諸兒書論家世集云：「史傳稱安平崔氏及汝南應氏，並累世有文才，所以范蔚宗云崔氏『世擅雕龍』。

translations.literal: " He also wrote to his sons discussing the family's collected writings, saying: "Historical records say the Cui clan of Anping and the Ying clan of Runan both had literary talent through successive generations; therefore Fan Ye said of the Cui clan, 'For generations they monopolized the carving of dragons.'"
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote to his sons about the family's literary collections: "Historical records say that the Cui clan of Anping and the Ying clan of Runan both produced literary talent for generations; that is why Fan Ye said of the Cui clan, 'For generations they monopolized the carving of dragons.'"

sentences.zh: 然不過父子兩三世耳；

translations.literal: Yet that was no more than two or three generations of father and son;
translations.idiomatic: Yet that amounted to no more than two or three generations of fathers and sons;

sentences.zh: 非有七葉之中，名德重光，爵位相繼，人人有集，如吾門世者也。

translations.literal: They did not have, within seven generations, fame and virtue shining again, ranks succeeding one another, every man with a collection, like our clan through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: They did not have, across seven generations, fame and virtue renewed in succession, offices passed from father to son, and every man with a collected work, as our house has.

sentences.zh: 沈少傅約語人云：『吾少好百家之言，身爲四代之史，自開闢已來，未有爵位蟬聯，文才相繼，如王氏之盛者也。

translations.literal: Junior Mentor Shen Yue told people: "From youth I loved the teachings of the hundred schools; I have personally been historian through four dynasties; since the opening of the age there has never been such succession of rank after rank and literary talent after literary talent as the flourishing of the Wang clan."
translations.idiomatic: Junior Mentor Shen Yue once said: "From youth I loved the teachings of the hundred schools; I have served as historian through four dynasties; since the beginning of history there has never been such unbroken succession of rank and literary talent as in the flourishing of the Wang clan."

sentences.zh: 』汝等仰觀堂構，思各努力。

translations.literal: " You should look up at the hall's framework and think to each exert yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: " Look up at the hall our forebears built, and strive each in your own way.

sentences.zh: 」筠自撰其文章，以一官爲一集，自洗馬、中書、中庶子、吏部、左佐、臨海、太府各十卷，《尚書》三十卷，凡一百卷，行於世。

translations.literal: " Yun himself compiled his writings, making one collection for each office held: from Groom, Secretariat, Vice-Administrator, Personnel, Left Assistant, Linhai, and Minister Steward, ten volumes each; Memorials of the Ministry of Works thirty volumes—in all one hundred volumes, circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: " Yun compiled his own writings into collections named for each office he had held: ten volumes each for his terms as Groom, Secretariat Gentleman, Vice-Administrator, Personnel Director, Left Assistant, Prefect of Linhai, and Minister Steward, plus thirty volumes of Ministry of Works memorials—a hundred volumes in all, which circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 史臣陳吏部尚書姚察曰：王僧孺之巨學，劉孝綽之詞藻，主非不好也，才非不用也，其拾青紫，取極貴，何難哉！

translations.literal: The historian, Chen Minister of Personnel Yao Cha, said: Wang Sengru's vast learning, Liu Xiaochuo's literary ornament—the lord did not fail to love them, talent did not fail to be used; for them to pick up purple and blue robes and attain supreme honor—what difficulty was there!
translations.idiomatic: The historian Yao Cha, Minister of Personnel, writes: Wang Sengru's vast learning and Liu Xiaochuo's literary brilliance—their lord did not fail to appreciate them, nor were their talents left unused; for men like them to take purple and blue robes and reach the highest honors should have been easy!

sentences.zh: 而孝綽不拘言行，自躓身名，徒鬱抑當年，非不遇也。

translations.literal: Yet Xiaochuo did not restrain his speech and conduct; he himself stumbled in reputation and name, vainly suppressed in his prime years—it was not that he lacked favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xiaochuo would not restrain his words or conduct; he brought ruin on his own reputation and spent his best years in frustration—it was not that he lacked opportunity.

translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker in the source text.
